content: Zantrex-3 is an herbal dietary supplement produced by Zoller Laboratories, a subsidiary of Basic Research based in Salt Lake City, Utah. It is primarily marketed to individuals under the age of 30 through fast-paced television advertisements featuring athletic-looking individuals. The advertisements prominently claim that Zantrex-3 is America's number 1 selling weight loss pill. Ingredients The active ingredients in Zantrex-3 include Yerba Mate, Guarana, and standard caffeine. It is estimated that the pill contains an amount of caffeine equivalent to three to four cups of coffee. Additional ingredients include green tea extract, Damiana (a South American aphrodisiac), Schizonepeta, Ginseng, Maca root, Niacin, and Kola nut. Side Effects The potential side effects of Zantrex-3 are similar to those associated with excessive caffeine consumption. These side effects include: Jitters, anxiety, and increased sweating. Elevated heart rate and increased blood pressure. Nausea, stomachache, and diarrhea. Appetite suppression or loss of appetite. Cold sweats, restlessness, shaking, and irritability. Increased urination, as caffeine acts as a mild diuretic. Caffeine dependency, with the possibility of experiencing a crash when discontinuing the use of Zantrex-3. Niacin, a vasodilator, can cause uncontrollable swelling in various parts of the body in some cases. In severe instances, users may develop a condition known as angioedema. Criticism The marketing campaign for Zantrex-3 has been criticized for its lack of scientific evidence supporting its claims. One reviewer noted that if users adjust their diet, monitor caloric intake, and follow a practical exercise regimen, Zantrex-3 might provide an additional advantage. Pop Culture During the fifth season of VH1's Celebrity Fit Club, contestant Dustin Diamond initially gained five pounds. However, at the subsequent weigh-in two weeks later, he had lost the same five pounds. Diamond disclosed to the Fit Club panel that he had been taking Zantrex-3 and was pleased to have reversed the weight gain. At the final weigh-in, two weeks later, he had lost an additional thirteen pounds. Despite his weight loss, Diamond faced significant criticism from both the panel and his fellow contestants for using Zantrex-3 as a dietary supplement.
